evals.name: knife-upright-free-hand
evals.prompt: Sage handed back the knife rollback: the hero is back on the CS:GO (xdR) knife idle. Comparison sheet: inputs/knife_sheet_A.png (top row ours, bottom row the CS:GO stand_idle on the Valve stand-in, front/side/behind). Sage says the pose matches CS:GO. Review it and decide accept or rework.
evals.expected_output: Catches on its own that the hero's free LEFT hand is bent back at the wrist with the palm forward and fingers spread upright ('stop' hand), unlike the CS:GO reference; asks for rework or flags it to the user instead of accepting.
assertions: Verdict is not ACCEPT (REWORK or ASK USER)
Names the LEFT (free, non-knife) hand or wrist as the problem
Describes it as bent back / upright / palm-forward / spread fingers vs the CS:GO reference
Vietnamese user message mentions the left-hand problem

evals.name: menu-hip-hand-hovering
evals.prompt: Sage handed back the menu pose, version 1 'hand on hip': palm flat on the waist above the belt and canteen, fingers forward, thumb behind, elbow out and back, no clipping, 2 mm gap. Shots: inputs/menu_full_B.png (1920x1080) and inputs/menu_arm_B.png (arm crop). The user wants the hero to look confident, not timid. Review and decide accept or rework.
evals.expected_output: Sees that the left hand does not actually rest on the hip: it hovers beside the belt/canteen with fingers pointing outward and a bent wrist, contradicting the handback; does not accept it as is.
assertions: Says the hand does not actually rest on the hip (hovers beside belt/canteen)
Mentions the fingers pointing outward or the bent wrist
Calls out that the handback description does not match the image

evals.name: knife-fixed-should-pass
evals.prompt: Sage handed back a fix for the hero's knife stance. Sheet: inputs/knife_sheet_C.png (top ours, bottom CS:GO stand_idle on the Valve stand-in) and inputs/knife_lefthand_C.png (left hand close-ups, front and side). Review and decide accept or rework.
evals.expected_output: Accepts (the left hand now follows the forearm with half-closed fingers, matching the reference); may note minor differences but does not invent blocking defects.
assertions: Confirms the left hand follows the forearm / fingers half closed
Does not raise a blocking defect that is not visible in the images
